ohki1979_squid_perfusion@1.locator: Table 1a, p. 378, internal solution Id-1, seven artificial external solutions
ohki1979_squid_perfusion@1.preparation: Six Loligo pealii giant axons. Electrodes measured steady resting voltage during successive K-for-Na substitutions in a perfused axon at about 20 °C. The authors checked that the voltage returned near its initial level.
ohki1979_squid_perfusion@1.comparison: The forward projection transfers the 1949 relative permeabilities and uses the nominally chloride-free and sodium-free internal recipe. Fluoride, phosphate, calcium and electrode effects are outside the three-current model. Only voltage changes are compared. The two-anchor interpolation uses the 10 and 350 mM means, with the interior means held out and 500 mM reported separately.
ohki1979_squid_perfusion@1.uncertainty: Reported ± for the six successful axons. Table 1 gives no definition of these errors or covariance between solution means. Electrode-tip corrections were applied, up to about 3 mV.

kapus1993_macrophage_proton@1.locator: Table II, symmetric Cs-aspartate rows, and Fig. 8 on pH changes during prolonged depolarization
kapus1993_macrophage_proton@1.preparation: Native mouse peritoneal macrophages, whole-cell proton tail currents at approximately 22 °C. Voltage is cell interior relative to bath.
kapus1993_macrophage_proton@1.uncertainty: Table II reports means ± SEM. Estimated residual junction offsets below 6 mV were uncorrected. The intracellular dye indicated good initial dialysis and a rise in pH of up to 0.8 during a 9 s pulse in a separate experiment.

morihata2000_microglia_proton@1.locator: Figure 2B–C, reversal from proton current tails
morihata2000_microglia_proton@1.preparation: Native rat microglia, pipette pH 5.5, bath pH stepped across four solutions. Temperature 22–24 °C. Voltage is cell interior relative to bath.
morihata2000_microglia_proton@1.uncertainty: Means and SEMs read approximately from the figure. The 45 mV/pH slope over the first three baths is printed in the text. Liquid junction potential was corrected before sealing. Intracellular pH at tail measurement was unmeasured.

fedorenko2012_ucp1_reversal@1.locator: Figure 1F, reversal across gradients, and Fig. 6E, an example with two bath pH values
fedorenko2012_ucp1_reversal@1.preparation: Mouse brown-adipose mitoplasts with UCP1-associated current. Figure 6E used bath oleic acid and 15 mM pipette α-cyclodextrin to impose asymmetric fatty-acid availability. Voltage is matrix relative to bath.
fedorenko2012_ucp1_reversal@1.uncertainty: Approximate crossings in Fig. 6E lack individual voltage error estimates. The manuscript Results and Fig. 6E caption disagree on the bath oleic-acid unit, so its concentration is excluded from the comparison. The separate multi-gradient comparison in Fig. 1F used 3–10 recordings per condition and a 24 °C Nernst reference. This study and the 2019 skeletal-muscle study share the Kirichok laboratory.

revilla1999_cx43_kinetics@1.locator: Figure 3A–C and Results, wild-type rat Cx43 homotypic junctions
revilla1999_cx43_kinetics@1.preparation: Paired Xenopus oocytes. Untagged rat Cx43 on both sides. Same publication as the registered Cx43 steady-conductance fits.
revilla1999_cx43_kinetics@1.uncertainty: Reported rounded ratio. The paper presents kinetic and conductance series from six pairs. No separate sampling interval for this amplitude ratio.

sahu2013_cx43_clamp@1.locator: Table 2, wild-type Cx43 row, Fig. S2 and Results on current decay
sahu2013_cx43_clamp@1.preparation: Homotypic Cx43 in N2a cell pairs, transjunctional step to −100 mV for kinetics.
sahu2013_cx43_clamp@1.uncertainty: Means ± SEM for seven pairs. These are fitted time constants in a fixed-voltage clamp.

desplantez2011_cx43_kinetics@1.locator: Results on current deactivation and Table 3, wt-Cx43/wt-Cx43 row
desplantez2011_cx43_kinetics@1.preparation: Homotypic untagged Cx43 in paired HeLa cells, dual whole-cell clamp at 22–25 °C. The fast and slow contributions are fractions of the initial decaying component.
desplantez2011_cx43_kinetics@1.uncertainty: Table 3 reports mean ± SEM across seven pairs. The WT fast time-constant comparison in their Fig. 5 and Table 2 reuses their 2004 series. The authors describe slow time constants as difficult to estimate.

strack2011_achr_two_components@1.locator: Table 2, innervated adult mouse muscles, fitted components
strack2011_achr_two_components@1.preparation: Labelled AChR in innervated tibialis anterior. The two-component fit is normalized at day 2. The pre-existing claim's Fig. 3D uses a day-7 anchor in the same study.
strack2011_achr_two_components@1.uncertainty: Table 2 means and SD for ten muscles. These fitted components and the Fig. 3 observations have common provenance.

stanley1983_achr_turnover@1.locator: Primary report, Science 222, 67–69, abstract with component estimates
stanley1983_achr_turnover@1.preparation: Normally innervated mouse diaphragm neuromuscular junctions.
stanley1983_achr_turnover@1.uncertainty: Published component estimates. The public abstract gives no pointwise time series, errors or sample counts. The inferred subpopulation fractions are approximate.

bruneau2010_active_achr@1.preparation: Active adult mouse sternomastoid synapses. Fewer than 20% of AChRs labelled, muscle fibers expressing rapsyn–GFP.
bruneau2010_active_achr@1.uncertainty: Values and times from Results (SD). The figure caption specifies SEM for the plotted bars. Two follow-ups cannot identify the decay law.

ohno2002_achr_count_current@1.locator: Table 2 and footnotes. Patient 3 and controls for the adult comparison
ohno2002_achr_count_current@1.preparation: Human intercostal endplates. A receptor-scaffold deficiency reduced available binding sites. Miniature endplate currents were recorded at −80 mV and 22 ± 0.5 °C.
ohno2002_achr_count_current@1.uncertainty: Table reports SE. No error or replicate count for this patient’s binding-site estimate. The measurements were not linked by individual endplate. Endplate geometry, local opening and transmitter exposure could differ. Patient 4 was a child and has no age-matched site count in the table.

bruneau2005_achr_recycling@1.locator: Figure 7A–B and Results, days 1 and 4 after transient receptor block
bruneau2005_achr_recycling@1.preparation: Adult mouse sternomastoid endplates. Repeat surface labelling distinguishes previously exposed receptors that resurfaced from newly inserted receptors.
bruneau2005_achr_recycling@1.uncertainty: Four-day values and SDs from Results. The graph shows SEM. The denominator is the initial surface fluorescence. The study did not measure the final size of the internal receptor pool or the area of membrane returned.
